idiom_name: TaskGroup workers over an actor-guarded channel
implementation_notes: Swift has no multi-consumer queue in the standard library - AsyncStream is single-consumer by design and a TaskGroup runs a fixed batch of child tasks - so the pool is assembled: an actor (or Mutex) guards a buffer that N child tasks in a withTaskGroup loop drain until the channel closes. Structured concurrency gives the pattern the pieces it needs - cancellation propagates from the group to every worker, and child tasks cannot outlive the group - while the queue semantics, acknowledgement and redelivery stay the application's or a broker client's responsibility.
pitfalls: A second consumer over one AsyncStream does not compete - each iterator sees the same sequence, so the extra worker silently duplicates or starves; you need an explicit queue.
TaskGroup cancellation stops all workers mid-flight: make handlers cancellation-aware (check Task.isCancelled) and treat abandoned work as redeliverable.
An actor holding the queue serialises dequeue for everyone; keep the critical section minimal or the pool degenerates into a queue of waiters.

variants.name: Foundation OperationQueue with maxConcurrentOperationCount
variants.implementation_notes: Foundation's older work-queue abstraction maps one-to-one onto the pattern: enqueue Operations onto an OperationQueue whose maxConcurrentOperationCount is n, and the queue schedules at most n at a time, each Operation running exactly once; dependencies, cancellation and QoS are built in. It predates structured concurrency and remains the pragmatic choice when competing consumers are Foundation operations (downloads, batch items) rather than broker messages.
pitfalls: OperationQueue is still supported but not the direction of the platform: prefer structured concurrency for new code unless dependencies/cancellation semantics are needed.
Blocking inside an Operation occupies one of the n slots; a synchronous network call in every operation reduces the pool to its slowest path.
Cancelled operations are simply not started (or must check isCancelled) - an item cancelled mid-flight is dropped, not redelivered.
